title: Start here
body: Open a section from the grouped menu, then choose the record you need. Save before leaving a form. A saved confirmation means the portal accepted that change; it does not automatically mean work is approved. If someone changed a record while you were editing, reopen the current page. Use Help with this page for the relevant guide. Search help by what you want to do, such as submit work, review, alerts or employer. Within a profile, the main action and frequent links stay visible. Open More actions for grouped learning, support and administration links allowed for your account. On My next step, start with the task shown; progress and account options are grouped below it. On a narrow screen, detailed tables scroll within their own area. Save an unfinished form before following a link. Progress reporting starts with headline figures. Select one to see matching records, then open a chart’s Exact figures table for the values. Attendance uses its displayed date period; task decisions and plan references are current at capture. Open How these figures are calculated for definitions. Missing information stays Not available. CSV/JSON exports recheck your current permissions. Demonstration screens and exports are marked fictional and never save to live records.

title: Understand the figures
body: Task approval, training-topic completion and qualification achievement are separate. A percentage describes only the records named beside it. Missing information stays unknown. Overdue items need action; a reference date is not always a booked appointment. Open the source before drawing a conclusion. Recorded OTJ hours are the valid loaded subtotal and may not be complete historical evidence. No overall apprenticeship achievement or inspection grade is inferred.

title: Set up your account, staff and assignments
body: Use Portal setup for the order of work. Martin provisions the first named Admin or CEO account. Add staff once, using their work email and primary role, and use staff onboarding to arrange their own sign-in. Assign each apprentice a tutor, Learning and Progress Mentor, Careers adviser and required Maths and English tutors. Additional staff duties can be recorded separately. Inclusion access is controlled in Support permissions. A staff Manager role is not an administrator account. Directory buttons now name the record: Add employer, Add programme, Add tutor group or Add staff member. Check existing records and clear search/status filters before creating another. On each saved directory record, What to do next links to the relevant assignments or account setup. A staff role does not itself create a caseload or invitation.

title: Add and reopen an apprentice
body: Create the employer, programme, tutor group and staff records first where needed. Add the apprentice using their learner reference and known details. Check programme version, dates and named staff, then reopen the saved profile. Link the correct individual apprentice login. Choose alert preferences and verify contacts before any sending. Assign training tasks explicitly. Saving a profile does not approve a training plan, RPL assessment or qualification result. If a choice is missing, open Missing employer, programme, group or staff choices for the setup links. You can save known apprentice details and reopen Edit apprentice for remaining optional assignments. The saved profile has What to do next links for details, training tasks and the separate apprentice sign-in setup. Do not create a second apprentice profile because tasks or a login are missing. When you reopen the profile, Check details and assignments is the main action. Frequent task, review, support and attendance links stay visible. More actions contains Administration, including Set up apprentice sign-in and Verify employer access.

title: Choose staff duties and responsibilities
body: A primary role and additional duties are separate. Administration can assign Careers, Learning and Progress Mentor, Maths or English duties to eligible staff, then link the correct people to apprentice profiles. Inclusion permissions have their own scope controls. My responsibilities brings together work available through current assignments. Old assignments and inactive accounts do not grant continuing access.

title: Submit work
body: Open your tasks from My next step or your training page. Save a draft while working. Add the required evidence and a short explanation, then confirm the work is your own and submit. Submitted work is locked for checking. If referred, read the tutor feedback, correct the original task and resubmit. Extra uploads do not approve the task. A whole-task approval, topic completion and qualification result remain separate. If a status filter shows no results, choose Show all assigned tasks before assuming your tasks are missing. Save your answers before adding evidence because these are separate forms. What happens next explains the recorded task state. Referred tasks show the most recent recorded referral feedback near the top; read the history or ask the Tutor if feedback is missing. Your dashboard keeps unavailable tasks under Checks / Tutor follow-up: missing programme source, an unreleased block or a paper assessment. The recorded deadline remains; this does not make the work complete or change the plan. Read the reason and ask the Tutor. On a closed block, saved work can be read but the existing release controls still apply. Paper assessments are arranged/recorded by the Tutor and cannot be submitted as online apprentice work.

title: Your next step
body: My next step shows available work, saved training sessions, review references and outstanding actions. A review due reference is not an appointment booking. Use the questionnaire and review sign-off links when requested. Your journey shows recorded milestones rather than guessing completion. If something is missing, ask the responsible member of staff. Do not enter a guessed result or date. The achievement timeline now also brings together your next action, saved training day, published review booking and separate due reference. The vehicle marks dated recorded milestones, including checked review meetings, rather than future plans. A shortcut takes you to the latest recorded point. A valid saved roster can include your profile number as a number or text; cancelled, ended or invalid sessions are not selected as your next training day. My next step now shows a current published review appointment separately from the ten-week due reference, using the same checks as the journey page. Open the appointment to check details and respond; a booking is not attendance or signing. What is left before Gateway shows only the current approved configured checks. Missing and To check are different. Follow an outstanding check to its section. No current approved criteria means preparation is not assessed, not that everything is complete. The dashboard work list now explains source, block-release and paper-assessment follow-up as checks. These are separate from tasks you can currently complete online. Your original source deadlines remain visible and need the Tutor’s attention; the check label does not change the plan or complete the work. Start with the next task or action at the top. My tasks, My calendar, I need help and reviews waiting for your sign-off stay visible. Open My progress and account options for reports, reminders and your achievement timeline. My progress shows approved tasks against saved task deadlines, with work awaiting tutor marking separate. Your next step opens the existing task or action. OTJ, attendance, topic completion and qualifications remain separate; missing plan dates do not create an on-track judgement.

title: Add photo evidence
body: Use your phone to open the relevant task and choose its evidence upload. Take or select a suitable workplace photo, add a short explanation and link it to the right task. Check that people or unrelated personal information are not visible. Uploading a photo does not submit or approve the whole task. The tutor checks whether it supports the task; keep the original work description clear.

title: Mark work and register attendance
body: Use the marking worklist to open current submitted tasks. Check the whole task and record your decision and useful feedback in the original task. Marking is overdue after more than seven calendar days; missing or future submission dates need checking. A reminder marked seen does not approve work. For registers, record actual attendance, delivered subjects and time rather than expected learning. An empty task status filter does not mean no tasks are assigned. Clear the filter to see the existing allocation; the unfiltered approval summary is labelled separately. Paper assessment results are recorded through the paper test fields, not inferred from an upload. The task page explains whether the work is awaiting a decision or already approved. Dashboard checks now distinguish missing sources, unreleased blocks and paper assessments from available overdue apprentice work. Source required tasks remain visible for source follow-up. The staff attention list uses the same distinction for due paper/blocked tasks. A check label does not amend dates or clear the original plan. Use the existing source, assessment, deadline or authorised release workflow; no control is bypassed. On a profile, Open training tasks is the main tutor action. Progress reviews, attendance and the permitted support or concern link stay visible. Reference and source details on the task list contains occasional reference links.

title: Set a SMART action
body: Agree one clear outcome, a measurable or observable success criterion, relevance, support, named owner and a realistic due date. To do, With tutor and Completed mean different things. Referred-task actions link to the original task and follow its source status. Use existing targets when relevant rather than duplicating them in a review. A suggested action is not an agreed target until the responsible people check and accept it.

title: Topics and qualifications
body: Open Maths and English, find the apprentice and open their subject record. Authorised subject staff can use Add qualification for the chosen start date and qualification details, Record / update a result to find an existing qualification, or Assign a training topic for assessed learning needs. Use zero planned hours only where knowledge is secure. Topic evidence acceptance, tutor-confirmed topic completion and qualification achievement are separate. Record the actual qualification result; a topic percentage or uploaded certificate does not automatically record a pass.

title: Release training blocks
body: New task allocations can use sequence controls. A later block opens after the five source tasks in each earlier block are approved. Administration can record a reasoned exception through block controls. That exception releases work; it does not approve the task, a KSB, the programme or a training plan. Existing task sets stay as saved until their sequence controls are explicitly changed.

title: Repeat a plan or correct a register
body: Repeated weekly session plans create separate saved rosters and empty registers. Check closures, holidays and actual attendance for each session. To correct a saved register, reopen it with a reason and save the corrected actual information. Previous marks stay in history. New valid minutes replace the old subtotal; overlapping training cannot be counted twice.

title: Record additional training
body: Record actual additional training, its time, exclusions, new learning and evidence in the existing training workflow. Outside normal hours needs the apprentice agreement and evidence of compensation where required by that record. Pending or withdrawn records do not add hours. Overlapping recorded time cannot count twice. Compare valid loaded hours with the approved individual plan, and check gaps or missing historical sources rather than inventing hours.

title: Prepare a review draft
body: Open Reviews, find the apprentice and choose Start review / View history, or Continue latest draft. Review appointments is for arranging the meeting; Review signing is for participant sign-off records. Save a draft before generating factual preparation notes. Check the selected source notes, complete the actual discussion, participation, judgement and targets, save again and complete preparation checks. Mark the checked saved content Ready for signatures, then prepare participant sign-off from that review. Booking a meeting or saving a draft does not complete a review or reset its deadline. Externally signed copies use their separate upload and independent-check process. The Review stages panel summarises the draft, saved preparation, frozen source and participant sign-off steps. Read the saved-version preparation checklist; typed changes are not included until saved. A PDF download or Ready for signatures status does not complete a review.

title: Read and sign your review
body: Open Review signing and Waiting for me. Read the same participant record and selected actions that the other named participants see. Type your recorded name, confirm this is your own decision and re-enter your current password. Decline with a private reason to GTA if the record needs correcting. All signed still needs an independent staff check. After checking, the original PDF is available. A withdrawn record keeps its history and is no longer a current completed-review reference.

title: Release and check a review record
body: Prepare participant sign-off from a complete frozen review and current employer signing authority. Check every shared field and selected action before explicit release. Restricted support fields are excluded, but other free text still needs privacy checking. Each of the three participants uses their own account and password. A different administrator or CEO checks the three decisions and source before confirmation. Only that check creates the retained PDF and activates the actual meeting plus seventy days reference.

title: Verify employer signing authority
body: First verify the named employer account and its apprentice access. Record separate review-signing authority using actual identity and workplace-authority evidence and an expiry date. Ordinary employer reply access is not signing authority. Renewal, revocation, changed account or expiry can block pending review packets. Reconcile them explicitly rather than reusing another person or silently resetting signatures. Use the Employer setup guide to distinguish an employer organisation record, a named contact login, an invitation and per-apprentice workplace authority. An organisation email does not automatically create any of those account permissions.

title: Complete a portal questionnaire
body: Open Questionnaires, then the portal questionnaire worklist. Apprentices can save an incomplete private draft; the Inclusion Team sees its status but cannot read unfinished answers. Read the privacy information and submit explicitly when ready. A returned response has a message explaining what to check; resubmission keeps the previous response. Ongoing wellbeing is voluntary and has no deadline or overdue flag. For urgent help, speak directly to GTA staff rather than waiting for this inbox.

title: Manage questionnaire submissions
body: Use the native questionnaire worklist within your current Inclusion scope. Assign an approved form revision and deliberate cycle reference; repeating the same form series and cycle does not duplicate it. Check only the latest submitted response, keep private notes separate from the apprentice message, and record follow-up. Link only a concern for the same apprentice. Resolve linked concerns in their original records before closing questionnaire follow-up. Form wording needs an authorised author and a different manager to publish it.

title: Use an external questionnaire link
body: Some questionnaires still open on an external service in a new tab. Read that service privacy information before answering. Opening a link does not record submission or completion in the portal. The Inclusion Team reconciles external receipts separately. Native portal submissions and old external receipts are not automatically merged. Use the questionnaire you have actually been asked to complete.

title: Follow up a concern
body: Open Support and retention. Search by apprentice name or reference, then choose Start / manage support; apprentices without a concern or plan are included. In the support record, check inclusion markers. An administrator or Inclusion Team lead can add or change them. Record the support need as a concern if no relevant concern exists. The lead or administrator selects its marker, owner and next action. Create a support-plan draft once a relevant concern is classified, or continue the current plan. Save the draft before requesting approval. Markers alone do not create or approve a plan. Record delivered support and reviews in the approved plan. Keep teaching instructions separate from private notes; do not record safeguarding case details here. Keep the support record focused on four points: the apprentice’s own view of what would help; what has changed with a practical example of whether support is working; the next agreed action with a named person and deadline; and why support closes with any support that should continue afterwards. Use the existing plan view, impact/evidence, review notes and closure boxes. Concern follow-ups already have action, owner and deadline fields. Do not duplicate an existing action or invent the apprentice’s view. Older notes remain historical notes, not newly assigned tasks. Review notes and agreed next steps are now visible in the restricted review history. If no ongoing support or next action is needed, record that clearly.

title: Ask GTA for help
body: Use My help and achievements to send a task-help, employer-issue or private-support request to the appropriate team. Check your portal receipt and later response. It is not a continuously monitored emergency channel. Private support is restricted to the appropriate Inclusion team. For urgent help, speak directly to GTA staff. An achievement you record enters the checked journey only after the appropriate staff decision.

title: Record advice
body: Open Careers, search for the apprentice, then use Find an apprentice / Open careers record to reach the apprentice list. Open their careers record even if there are no outstanding actions. The administrator or assigned authorised adviser can use Record a careers discussion, choose career progression or employment support, and record the actual date, goals, advice and outcome. Save the discussion, then add agreed measurable actions with an owner and deadline. Employers cannot access private careers records. A seen prompt does not prove advice was delivered.

title: Use the employer action centre
body: Employers open their own action centre to see specific requests shared with their verified account. Read the request and give the appropriate confirmation, change request or cannot-confirm response. A workplace confirmation does not approve an OTJ claim or qualification. Review content responses are separate from participant review signatures. GTA checks replies in the original workflow. Access ends when the employer grant or current authority no longer applies. Reviews waiting for my sign-off and Workplace support summaries shared with me stay at the top of My employer actions. Open request and reply opens a shared request; replying is separate from signing a review. Progress reporting shows currently authorised shared requests. A named employer request grant does not open full attendance, tasks, support or careers records. Reviews awaiting my input opens the separate checked signing workflow.

title: Choose text and email alerts
body: Open Alert preferences to choose email, text, both or off. Keep contacts correct and complete the required verification; an entered phone number alone is not verified. GTA recommends keeping useful reminders on, but you can change your preferences. Generic reminders link back to your portal rather than sending task answers or private support details. An accepted delivery attempt is not proof that a message reached or was read on your phone.

title: Manage apprentice reminders
body: Open Apprentice reminder delivery to preview eligible source items and prepared attempts. Current consent, verified contacts, approved recipient lists, programme status, budgets and pause controls apply. Prepare stores a digest without sending; explicit dispatch or an enabled schedule is separate. Pause this pipeline when investigating. Accepted is transport acceptance, not inbox or handset proof. Never reset a reserved, uncertain or rejected attempt to force a resend.

title: Staff development privacy
body: Open your own Staff development records and CPD. Assigned line managers and the CEO have the appropriate management access. Ordinary administrator access does not automatically expose another employee private HR information. A planned meeting and a completed linked record are different states. Use evidence and recorded outcomes; do not turn an unobserved activity into a judgement.

title: Show evidenced impact
body: Create an anonymous case study using its structured fields. Do not copy personal, health or safeguarding details. Record the starting point, response, evidenced difference, limitations and next check. A different administrator or CEO approves the exact version before it can appear in the internal inspection overview. Internal approval is not permission for external publication.

title: Reporting
body: Operational reports link to connected source records. Retention and achievement are different measures. Unknown or incomplete historical data is shown explicitly. Management snapshots record the sources available at capture and do not silently change when source records change later. Open underlying records before acting on a flag. The inspection overview is partial evidence, not an inspection grade.

title: Change your password and confirm your email
body: Use Change password with your current password and a new passphrase of at least twelve characters. You will be signed out and older sessions are invalidated. Confirm your own email through the account workflow when requested. Staging recovery and invitation delivery need the configured mail service and actual mailbox acceptance. Ask GTA if access cannot be verified. Pending review signing may need a fresh source check after an account change.

title: Choose help audio
body: Read the transcript on this page at any time. If an approved GTA Yorkshire recording is available, press Play GTA recording; it starts only when you choose. Stop or pause it using the player. Device read-aloud is a separate option whose accent depends on your device. No microphone is used. Only these general help guides are read, never apprentice records. Ask GTA to check missing or outdated guidance rather than reading private record information into an audio service.

title: Emergency access
body: Ordinary CEO oversight does not need emergency override. Use emergency access only when required, with a recorded reason, your current password and acknowledgement of the audit. It applies to the current session and ends on sign-out or explicit end. Current source, version, inactive-account and normal safety checks still apply.

title: Finding the right action
body: Open Quick actions and search for what you want to do, such as a support plan, results or evidence. Choose a task, then find the apprentice by name or reference. Only records in your current access appear. Other actions for this apprentice keeps the same person while you choose a different section. Opening these pages does not create a record. If an apprentice is missing, check your search and ask an administrator to check the current assignment. Existing role, approval and save checks still apply. On an apprentice profile, frequent actions stay visible and More actions groups the remaining permitted links. On the task list, Reference and source details holds curriculum links. Expand these sections with a tap, click or keyboard; they open within the page.

title: Checking an apprentice record
body: Open Apprentice record checks to find missing programme, employer, group, tutor, account or learning-date links. Open the record to check current active accounts, matching duties, allocated tasks and the provider-approved delivery plan. Recorded means that the stated source check passed; it does not mean qualification achievement, Gateway readiness, funding approval or successful sign-in. Missing maths or English assignments require a check of the assessed training need, not an assumed exemption. An administrator can correct profile links; tutors can open the original training sources or ask for a correction.

title: Adding a workload to the timetable
body: As an authorised planner or administrator, open Centre timetable in the Manage view and choose Add workload, either at the top or in a staff/date cell. Choose staff, activity type, a generic title, dates, times and site. Teaching also needs the assigned group Tutor, a suitable room and expected headcount. For a year-long pattern choose up to53 weekly dates within the coming year; enter holiday or excluded dates where needed. Save draft. On the next page review every date and any errors or warnings, check the exact draft, then publish it. Saving a draft does not place a published card on the timetable. Before publication, use Working time to record checked staff availability and Rooms to confirm room use/capacity. Unknown time is not free time. If the card is missing, check Manage versus My timetable or Staff timetable, the selected week/staff/site and whether the plan is still a draft. Workload plans do not record attendance, off-the-job training or completed work. Keep personal support and medical details out of shared activity titles.

title: Changing workloads and using optional drag-and-drop
body: Open Centre timetable in Manage view. Use Add workload in a staff/date cell or Move workload in the accessible item list. Optionally tick Enable optional drag-and-drop shortcuts. Drag a work type into a staff/date cell to open a prefilled new draft. Drag an existing planned card into a staff/date cell to open a requested move; the current start time is retained until you edit it on the form. Dropping never saves or moves work automatically. Check the exact proposed date, person and time, save the checked proposal for review, then confirm arrangements and apply. If you decide against it, cancel the saved proposal and the original workload stays reserved. Use full-year planning for repeated activities. Registered, protected, partly delivered or cover-linked activities can be held and need their original plan/register/cover workflow. Recorded delivery and attendance are never rewritten by dragging. Teaching keeps the primary group Tutor; use reviewed teaching cover rather than changing apprentice responsibility. The normal buttons and forms remain available for keyboard, touch and users who do not wish to drag.

title: Planning the full year and reviewing an automated proposal
body: Open Plan the full year from the centre timetable. Choose a period within the next year, optionally filter staff and select the future published plans to consider together. Create recurring activities and confirm their dated working windows first. You can nominate alternative rooms at the original site. For Admin, Preparation and Staff development you can nominate suitable alternative staff; marking and private apprentice responsibilities remain with their existing owners. Choose original dates, dates within seven days or any checked start date in the selected year. Teaching dates change only when you explicitly allow it, and the assigned Tutor/group remain fixed. Review every original/proposed date, person and room, and the warnings. Confirm nominated staff suitability and record agreed arrangements, then save for final review. Nothing has moved. Apply the exact reviewed proposal within30 minutes; a changed source or authority blocks it and requires a new preview. All changes apply together or none apply. You can cancel before application. The bounded search suggests a complete checked schedule but does not prove a globally best timetable. It never assumes unknown working time is available, changes attendance/OTJ or sends messages automatically. Up to128 plans/5000 occurrences can be reviewed per batch; all other current work remains a constraint.

title: Set up an employer organisation and named contact
body: First check the Employers directory for the organisation, including inactive records or search filters, before using Add employer. That record is used on apprentice profiles. Its workplace contact email does not create a portal account. Open Employer accounts to create the individual named contact login if needed. Creating it sends no invitation and grants no apprentice access. Review the contact record, arrange the controlled invitation only when the configured service is ready, and verify workplace authority for each relevant apprentice. Mailbox confirmation alone is not employer authority. Review-signing authority is a separate checked step. Use the saved organisation record What to do next links to apprentice assignments or named employer contacts. If a person or organisation is missing from a filtered list, clear the filters before adding a duplicate. Never use another person’s login or assume one employer contact can see all apprentices.

title: Follow the apprenticeship road map
body: Open the apprentice record and Apprenticeship journey to see dated recorded milestones. The GTA lorry is selected for a linked active Heavy Vehicle programme. The GTA car is selected for linked active Light Vehicle, Autocare, Panel and Paint programmes. Other, unlinked or inactive programmes use a neutral marker; no programme or training source is guessed. The marker identifies the latest valid recorded milestone date already included in this road map. Future dates do not advance it. It is not a percentage complete, elapsed-time measure, Gateway decision or EPA result. Several milestones may share a date. With motion enabled, the vehicle travels briefly from the preceding displayed point and rests at the current point with a gentle pulse. Use Pause marker animation to stop it; resuming restarts the pulse without replaying travel. Reduced-motion preferences keep it still. Without scripting the marker remains static at the recorded point. Printed records retain the latest-point text without animation. Private support and Careers records remain excluded, and source links retain their usual permissions. What happens next separates the next available action, saved training day and current published review appointment from dated milestones. A booked meeting does not confirm availability, attendance or signing. The due reference is ten weeks after a reliable checked review meeting and is not a booking. Checked signed-review meeting dates can appear on the road; drafts, unconfirmed copies, withdrawn or damaged records cannot. The timeline shares only the meeting milestone, not participant signatures or private review text. Use Go to latest recorded point to avoid scrolling through the whole journey. Dates use day/month/year. Ask the Tutor if dates or sources need checking. The Gateway preparation summary shows up to three outstanding configured checks, with missing requirements before those still to check. Open the full list for the rest. All configured checks met still needs the separate provider Gateway review. This summary does not move the vehicle or grant approval.

title: Understand Gateway preparation checks
body: Open Gateway preparation from My next step, the journey or the apprentice profile. Start with What is left before Gateway. Missing means a configured requirement is not met; To check means its position is unknown or its source needs checking. Follow a named check to its exact section. The small summary shows up to three outstanding checks; the preparation page contains the full list. Only current independently approved programme/cohort criteria are used. If no current criteria are available, ask the Tutor to check the actual applicable standard, EPA plan and programme sources, prepare the six-category criteria and arrange a different Admin or CEO to approve them. Saved draft criteria are not approved criteria. A staff check must use the original source and the existing shareable note/reference confirmation. Changing source records can require manual checks to be repeated. Task approval, qualification achievement, evidence, KSB coverage, off-the-job training and agreements remain separate requirements. All configured checks met does not approve Gateway, establish funding compliance or book EPA. The provider and EPAO decisions remain separate. Never add or mark a criterion just to remove a warning. The summary shares check labels and status, not private review notes, signatures or hidden evidence. Use Help with this page if unsure.

title: Recruitment, entry and destination checks
body: From an apprentice profile choose Recruitment and starting circumstances. Record how they heard about GTA separately from how they obtained the job. At enrolment answer each question; Unknown and Prefer not to say remain honest responses. Family ownership alone does not mean the apprentice has relatives at work. Entry corrections require a brief reason; later employer or supervisor changes use the separate dated action. Never infer relationships from names. Use Retention administration for missing-data actions and 3, 6 and 12-month follow-up reminders. These administrative actions stay separate from urgent support. Confirm a sourced exit, then assign one administrator to all three checks from Outcome and reporting context or assign them separately in the follow-up list. Record actual contact result, destination, evidence basis and continuity in the existing leaver follow-up workspace. No reply needs a retry date and cannot establish employment. A later check retains earlier entries. A changed exit date supersedes old tasks without deleting their evidence. Compare recruitment factors in Retention analysis using programme, age, entry employer, prior employment and intake dates. Read counts, denominators and missingness together. Small samples are exploratory; a snapshot is not proof of sustained employment. Portal reminders do not send email or text.

title: Use employer and mentor resources
body: Use Employer & Mentor Resources for safeguarding contacts, reporting routes, practical mentoring guidance and your own topic progress across 23 topics and 46 quick checks. Reporting a concern or requesting apprentice support is never conditional on completing training. Named employer accounts and workplace mentors record their own reading, quick-check answers and explicit final commitments for their authorised organisation scope. Prior non-final topics must be recorded within the last 365 days before recording a commitment.
